title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative:
On May 23, 2023, the Employers’ Consultative Association of Trinidad and Tobago (ECA) initiated a public-private dialogue forum gathering ECA members alongside government representatives from various entities including the Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago, Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management (ODPM), Ministry of Youth Development and National Service, Ministry of Trade and Industry, Bureau of Standards and Ministry of Housing and Urban Development. The purpose was to discuss and debate a series of evidence-based business resilience policy proposal developed by the ECA in 2022. The ECA introduced two reports, “Perspectives on Business Resilience in Trinidad and Tobago" and "Business Resilience Trends and evidence-based-policy Proposals in Trinidad and Tobago", which outline prevailing business resilience patterns and areas necessitating improvements to enhance enterprise sustainability and survival amid unforeseen crises.
During this public-private dialogue, the ECA conveyed specific needs to enhance the resilience of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in Trinidad and Tobago. Subsequently, it maintained communication with the ODPM, the Chaguanas Chamber of Commerce, the Ministry of Youth Development, and the Ministry of Labour specifically concerning the revised SME policy with the National Service.
Parallel to its policy advocacy on business resilience, the ECA launched a new service titled “Sustainable and Resilient Enterprises (SURE)”. This service entails extending business resilience training and coaching to small and medium-sized enterprises. As of August 2023, the ECA delivered four training sessions, benefiting 24 companies and enabling them to formulate effective business resilience strategies. Between April 2022 and May 2023, the ILO supported the ECA to identify prevalent business resilience trends and policy priorities within the Trinidad & Tobago’s business community. This effort involved facilitating a nationwide online survey with 700 ECA members and conducting in-depth interviews with ten members. The ILO played a role in overseeing both primary and secondary research, in addition to delivering technical guidance for the formulation of policy proposals for submission to the government.
In relations to the rollout of ECA's new training service on SURE, the ILO conducted a training of trainers in July 2021, certifying five professional enterprise trainers associated with ECA. To enhance the visibility and uptake of SURE among Trinidad and Tobago’s enterprises, the ILO further assisted the ECA to market and promote SURE by developing a promotional video spotlighting SURE. Additionally, the ILO supported ECA in designing a dedicated SURE workplan concentrating on the delivery of SURE to small enterprises. Lastly, the ILO assisted the monitoring, evaluation and learning activities associated with the implementation SURE.
